title: Programs with multiple code files
recap: Each source file is compiled as an independent translation unit. A declaration in the calling file lets compilation proceed without exposing the implementation there.
The linker later connects calls to definitions from the other compiled source files. Every implementation file must therefore be included in the build rather than copied with an include directive.
objectives: Split a small program across two source files.
Declare a function implemented in another translation unit.
Compile and link every relevant source file.
Keep implementation files out of include directives.
warnings: Compiling only main.cpp leaves external function definitions unavailable to the linker.
Compilation order does not make declarations from one source file visible in another.
Including a .cpp file can create duplicate definitions and unnecessary rebuilds.
Each source file must include the library headers for the facilities it directly uses.
challenge: Implement requiredCrewHours in crew.cpp and declare it in main.cpp. Calculate whole crew hours for eight roof sections taking 45 minutes each, then print the exact report line.
hints: First, open crew.cpp and replace the placeholder calculation in requiredCrewHours; keep the existing matching declaration in main.cpp.

Pseudocode: IN main.cpp, DECLARE FUNCTION requiredCrewHours(sections: integer, minutesPerSection: integer) RETURNS integer. MAIN: hours = requiredCrewHours(8, 45); OUTPUT the crew-time label, hours, and hours suffix; return success. IN crew.cpp, DEFINE requiredCrewHours: totalMinutes = sections * minutesPerSection; RETURN totalMinutes / 60 using whole-number division.

Near-C++ structure: // main.cpp: int requiredCrewHours(int sections, int minutesPerSection) /* declaration terminator */ int main() { std::cout << /* label */ << requiredCrewHours(/* required arguments */) << /* suffix and newline */; /* return success */ } // crew.cpp: int requiredCrewHours(int sections, int minutesPerSection) { return /* multiply inputs, then divide by 60 */; }
